images.title: The Glasswind Rider
images.intent: A desert orc traveller and a new terrestrial mount: another possible culture and way of life beyond the familiar warband. Neither species biology nor faction is settled.

Keep the feathered bird's identity, plumage, beak, two-leg anatomy, pose, body scale and position exactly as in image 1. Preserve the pink salt flats, mesas, dramatic sky, original light and painted style. Rebuild the rider as a compact strong ADULT male goblin with the species anatomy of image 2: long prominently pointed ears, a narrow projecting nose, lively slightly hooded eyes, olive-ochre skin, a small angular chin and jaw, no orc underbite or tusks. images.creator_feedback: Revise this rider into a somewhat larger, stronger male goblin, still clearly goblin-like rather than orc-like. Point the spear forward. The completed revision awaits creator review.

Visual appeal: a beautiful, believable settlement tucked beneath living roots, where practical human architecture and immense woodland forms meet. Show a small inhabited quarter at the base of an ancient tree on a steep green hillside. Great gnarled roots arch naturally above limewashed stone rooms, timber balconies and red-brown tiled roofs; the tree is rooted solidly in the hill, not a floating island or giant humanoid. The root's immense curved mass and the intimate lit doorway make the composition; surrounding leaves and distant timberwork use quieter grouped marks. High fantasy inhabited by households with their own culture, not an idyllic theme park.

One living elderly gardener, small by comparison, passes the gate with a basket and briefly touches the wooden door, not hugging the machine or explaining it to us.
